chunks: And Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) about a man who buys food: Is his sale valid before he takes possession? He said:
"If he has profited (sold it for a profit), it is not valid until he takes possession; and if he assigns it (to another), there is no harm."

And he asked him about a man who buys food: Is it permissible for him to assign it before taking possession? He said: "If he has not profited from it by anything, there is no harm; but if he has profited, it is not valid until he takes possession."

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for selling food before taking possession in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the conditions of *bay' al-madmun* (sale of guaranteed goods) by distinguishing between a seller who has already secured a profit margin and one who has not; the former must take physical possession before reselling to avoid uncertainty (*gharar*), while the latter may delegate possession. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ensuring actual control over the commodity to validate the transaction, a principle rooted in the Prophetic tradition prohibiting the sale of what one does not possess.
